Might be obvious for some, but I just wanted to share a tiny little function I added to my .zshrc that might be handy for others:

function playNetMusic() { 
 if [ -n "$1" ]
 then 
 for link in $(cat $1)
 do mpv --no-video $link
 done 
 else 
 echo "Need input file with links to videos"
 fi 
}

Feed it a text document with youtube links you want to play the sound from (or anywhere else), and enjoy!

It shouldn't be too much hassle to write a little script to it that takes an artist as input and finds the youtube-links (or playlists) automatically, if anyone's up for it.
How to use youtube as a manual grooveshark-alternative.

You could also use youtube-dl which has a built-in search option. I have this bash function defined:

function pyt() {
 youtube-dl -q --max-downloads 1 --no-playlist --default-search ${2:-ytsearch} "$1" -o - | mplayer -vo null /dev/fd/3 3<&0 </dev/tty;
}

Used like this:

$ pyt "whole lotta love"
That's a nice one! Although some crazy plumbing going on at the end there.

I did something similar with youtube-dl:

for arg in "$@"
do
 if [ ${#arg} == 11 ]
 then
 vids=$vids" "$arg
 else
 flags=$flags" "$arg
 fi
done

for vid in $vids
do
 youtube-dl -f 18 -q -o- $vid | mplayer $flags -cache 4096 -
done

Wanted to be able to optionally pass in -vo null. A surprise is lurking for eleven-character mplayer arguments.
